title: Categorical classification of non-Fermi liquids in 2+1 dimensions
authors: Shubham Kukreja, Dawson M. Willerton, Sung-Sik Lee
abstract: A defining feature of non-Fermi liquids is a lack of the quasiparticle peak on the Fermi surface in the spectral function, which is usually realized by coupling a finite density of fermions with critical collective fluctuations. However, these features of the two- and three-point vertex functions are qualitatively the same across many non-Fermi liquids, which has made it difficult to classify them beyond the definition by negation. We point out that the four-point function in the pairing channel contains rich information that positively differentiates distinct types of non-Fermi liquids. Using the generalized notion of fixed points that captures scale-dependent universal pairing interaction, we provide a non-perturbative classification of 2+1-dimensional non-Fermi liquids. In the large Fermi momentum limit with fixed dimensionless couplings, metals coupled with long-wavelength critical fluctuations are classified into seven superuniversality classes. Each of them exhibits a unique phase diagram in the space of temperature and bare four-fermion coupling. The present work generalizes the earlier perturbative classification to strongly interacting non-Fermi liquids by leveraging kinematic constraints.
summary: This work tackles the challenge of classifying non-Fermi liquids in 2+1 dimensions by focusing on the four-point pairing function. Using a generalized Renormalization Group approach, the authors provide a non-perturbative classification, identifying seven distinct superuniversality classes. This offers a powerful theoretical framework for understanding strongly correlated quantum critical metals.
main_problem: The paper aims to develop a systematic classification of non-Fermi liquids (NFLs) in 2+1 dimensions, moving beyond merely defining them by what they are not.
main_result: The authors provide a non-perturbative classification of 2+1D NFLs, finding seven superuniversality classes based on the topology of the Renormalization Group (RG) flow.
method: The classification utilizes the four-point function in the pairing channel and analyzes the RG flow using a generalized notion of fixed points, extending perturbative methods non-perturbatively.
model_or_system: The system involves fermions coupled to critical collective fluctuations in 2+1 dimensions, relevant to quantum critical metals and superconductivity near quantum critical points.
key_observables: The topological data of RG trajectories, the universal pairing interaction flow, and the resulting phase diagrams for each superuniversality class.
important_parameters: The large Fermi momentum limit ($k_F$), the ratio between the Cooper pair wavefunction pitch and the fluctuation momentum ($q_{\parallel}/k_F$), and the bare four-fermion coupling.
main_assumptions: The classification relies on the assumption that the topological features of the RG flow are robust and that high-energy modes decouple from low-energy physics.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate frequency scales and crossover mechanisms for the pairing interaction, show the flow of pairing interactions across different scales, and map out the RG flow generating mappings between couplings defining distinct superuniversality classes.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the difficulty in classifying NFLs, proposes using the four-point pairing function, develops the RG framework using generalized fixed points, and concludes by presenting the non-perturbative classification into seven superuniversality classes.
why_interesting: The rigorous, non-perturbative classification scheme based on RG topology is a powerful theoretical tool applicable to strongly correlated systems where standard mean-field or perturbative approaches fail.
